The 21st-century musician possesses the academic knowledge, skills, and habits that are keys to success in a rapidly changing world; he/she is also community-minded, inventive, and resourceful.

Founded in 1996 and inspired by the “spetsshkola” system of the former Soviet Union, Special Music School is a unique partnership between the New York City Department of Education and Kaufman Music Center, a not-for-profit cultural organization.

The visual arts program, provides students with the chance to explore various media such as painting, drawing, collage, recycling, and pottery. Our students participate in monthly and holiday assemblies that help to develop their knowledge and skills in the areas of acting and playwriting. The Move-To-Improve program engages students and enhancing their skills and techniques of dance and movement.

q44_1: Our current arts programs are embedded into our school curriculum and content studies. We ensure that every child has the opportunity to be involved in the arts program as a musician, singer, artist, director, stage hand, script writer, ballerina, or choreographer. Our goal is to expose our children to all arts forms as they continue to grow as learners at P.S. 1 and become well -rounded citizens in society.

During the 2016-2017 school year, students participated in choice art elective courses which included dance, african drumming and visual arts. At the beginning of the schoolyear, students completed opportunity to complete an art elective choice form to rank their art  preferences.  Students were placed in specific art sections based off of their preference choices. 90% of the students were granted their 1st preference, 7% were placed in theier 2nd choice and 3% in their 3rd choice.

PS 682 - is a Schoolwide Enrichment Model school. We conduct three nine week cycles of enrichment clusters ranging in areas from film-making, sports, horticulture, etc...based on student interests. TADA! for our K-5 students - students dance, sing, and act during the 20 week partnership. Dancing Classrooms for our 4th and 5th grade students, one cycle of ballroom dance lessons twice a week. We have one full-time music teacher trained in Music and the Brain. The 3-5 students have learned the recorder and our 4th and 5th grade students participate in band. We have a full-time art teacher, for art K-5. We continued Art History for grades 4 and 5. Also we have Town Hall in grades K-3, a Dance partnership. We have continued an after-school program that focuses on theater arts, visual arts, athletics, and computers. We are also a TC school that incorporates Art in ELA.

Our partnerships with Brooklyn Steppers, Arts Connection and Sheltering Arms have provided our scholars with the opportunity to explore the both music, theater, and visual arts in order to engage in a variety of projects and performances. Both our music and theater programs have added key enrichment opportunities for the young men of Eagle Harlem both during and after the school day.

The current arts program at Public School 40 is comprised of a weekly enrichment period that in which every child in P-KG to 5th grade engages in teacher-led arts activities spanning across genres of music, dance, theater, and visual arts. We also build on our existing program by offering dance to all of our students through a collaboration with a local art program, as we understand that a strong arts program will enhance our children's academic abilities.

The foundation of our social/emotional program is Choice Theory. The two needs we recognize as being essential for productive adolescent development are a sense of belonging and power or respect. These needs are fulfilled when students join clubs and develop competencies in the arts. We provide students with the opportunity to hone their knowledge and skills of fine arts and instrumental music. Also, our Media department offers video production provided by Urban Wall Street, which allows students to share their voice in a dynamic way. We collaborate with CAMBA to provide opportunities for students to learn the skills of choreography and dance, as well as audio/visual competencies.

As our student body has increased, so has our commitment to the arts.  This year, for the first time in many, we have a full time certified art teacher,and a certified full time music teacher. New this year was 3 rotations of Middle School arts clubs (based on student choice) which included film appreciation, 3D art, and band. Our long term (14 weeks and more) residency programs included Salvadori for Urban Design (MS) Landmarks, Memorials and Monuments, Music Together for PreK&K, Studio in A School for G4, Musical Theater from Wingspan & Main Street Theater for Grades 4&5, and African Dance from Main Street Theater for G3. Other grades participated in Hip Hop, Yoga/Movement, Ballroom Dance, Greek Architecture and Studio classes.  Additionally, we celebrated the arts with 3 Family Art Sat. and evening Workshops.
Unique to our building is our partnership with Cornell Tech Graduate School that has provided and supported arts learning through a year long residency program in computer science, that included several hack-a-thons for animation and game design and maker space events for a variety of design and arts projects. We continue our collaboration with the Main Street Theater and Dance Alliance, our own Roosevelt Island local arts community center.
We provided art for 10 G levels with 2 residency programs per
grade plus visual arts instruction and music through certified staff this year, hopefully, funding from our school budget and our parents through the PTA will enable us to do so again for 2017/2018 school year.

We are a PreK to 8 grade school on Roosevelt Island.
We are a diverse community of learners who speak over 17 different languages from over 30 countries who are in general education, special education and gifted and talented classrooms.  We have a very active PTA who is committed to providing funding for arts enrichment for all students across the school.

q44_1:
This year was another exciting year of art for students at PS 15, as we continue to expand our programs and partners (adding Puppetry this year). In addition, through implementation of the School-wide Enrichment Model, the faculty and staff have played an integral part in providing sustainable arts programming based on student-interest in clusters such as “Art for Change,” “Photography,” “Making Music” and “Trash to Treasure”. 
We continued residency programs with organizations such as The Children's Museum of Art, Mark DeGarmo Dance and Third Street Music, in which kindergarten through fifth grade students learned through the Orff Shulwerk approach. Students explored basic rhythms/melodies using various instruments. 
All our students visited arts museums, films and performances to supplement and extend arts learning objectives grown out of classroom curriculum. We continued our nine-year relationship with Arts for All, Inc, providing our kindergarten through second grade students with opportunities to integrate theater and visual art into literacy. Our students have many opportunities to express themselves through dance, music, and theater with our partnerships with Mark DeGarmo Dance, Rosie’s Broadway Kids, puppetry with Arts Connection and creative storytelling with Story Pirates. Lastly, through our Technology Arts class, students study mentor artists, learn coding, graphic design, and animation. We expect to have many submissions to this year’s District 1 Arts Fair and close the year on a high note for Arts at PS 15!

P.S. 119's goal is to provide arts instruction that facilitates self-expression and builds community spirit. Students are offered opportunities in all of the arts during our regular school day, weekday after school program, Next Jump, and our Literacy Through the Arts Saturday Program. One full-time visual art teacher, Resident Artist in Dance, Music, and Visual Arts, Project Boost, field trips to art institutions provided opportunities to all students at PS 119. Smartboards enable teachers to integrate the arts and technology. Students take virtual tours of world-renowned museums, attend performances, and study great works of art in the classroom and through outside field trips. We celebrate our diverse cultures through the performing and visual arts with annual festivities such as Fall, Winter and Spring concerts, special Mother's Day musical celebration, and Father/Daughter Dance. Social studies instruction includes an appreciation of the arts in each of the civilizations and cultures studied. Our Science Fair showcases student work demonstrating a rigorous integration of science, technology, social studies and visual arts. This years science fair theme was New York City based. Relationships with Dancing Classrooms, Smartworks, Music for Many, and New-York Historical Society have evolved over the years to permeate teaching practices. In the coming year we will expand the Arts Program to include Theatre Arts,and Choral Music during the day and/or after school programs.

q44_1: By June of 2018, students and staff will demonstrate an increased awareness of the arts. Participation in school and class concerts /performances, parent/student workshops and meeting grade appropriate benchmarks in the literacy of the arts strand as measured by The Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. Demonstration of mastery will be evidenced both within and beyond the classroom.

Our School Art’s Program for the fiscal year 2016-2017 comprises of the following:  

Teachers & Writers
During a T&W writing program, students come to think of themselves as writers. Most T&W workshops begin with students reading and discussing the work of contemporary and classic writers. Through these activities, students learn literary elements and techniques that they are then asked to use in their own creative writing—guided by a writing prompt assigned by the T&W writer. At the end of most T&W programs, students work with the writer to revise their work, which T&W publishes in an anthology and culminates at a celebrating event.

Studio in a School
The Studio in a School Residency Program is another program that is partners with us again this year. This community-based organizations offers customized art instruction for our students and caters for their particular needs. Residencies help our second through fourth grade students to build their foundational art skills and develop 21st century skills of communication and problem solving.

Creative Arts Team (CAT)

This is a Literacy through Drama (LTD) program which is new to us this year. Through this program, our students are exposed to drama.  In doing so, our participants are provided opportunities to explore social and academic literacy.

We have in class art lessons which art is incorporated across the curriculum. We presently are working with the Society of Educational Arts. We have had different assemblies programs that address different art disciplines. Grade performance that are done in the school.

We use the Blueprint for the Arts, and offer arts to all our students. One addition to our Arts program that we are proud of is the expansion of our Dramatic Arts Instruction. We have also increased our outreach to Cultural Organizations in order to enrich students understanding and appreciation of the arts disciplines.  We have nearly 33% English Language Learners. The arts is also a way of engaging our ELL students and motivating them to improve their use of the English language. Through the arts, we celebrate diversity in our school with cultural performances. In addition, the school runs a comprehensive architecture program for 7th graders. With the help of Mr. Ronald Miller, architect and director of Planning Design Construction for Maimonides Medical Center, classes use a life like request for proposals to design a building by preparing floor plans, elevation plans, axonometric drawings and a scale model. Ten final teams are chosen to represent the school of design Expo, a special day at the center for Architecture in Manhattan where the teams present their designs to a panel of professional architects.  Our school presents an annual festival of the Arts allowing students to showcase what they have learned through dramatic performances, musical concerts and exhibition of student art.  Parents of performing and exhibiting students are invited to attend.  Finally, we have also increased our after school and summer instruction in the Arts.

At P.S. 134 we strive to incorporate all aspects of the arts instruction into the curriculum. Our goal is to create a climate of appreciation and learning of all art forms by our students. We do this by exposing the students to various arts instruction from Kindergarten through Grade 5. We also do this by showcasing the accomplishments of all students in the arts. The students receive instruction in the arts from certified teachers who use the Blueprint for Teaching and Learning in the Arts to provide developmentally appropriate lessons. These teachers also differentiate instruction for the students to accelerate the learning of all students.

Our school enjoys an international reputation as the first and foremost high school dedicated to nurturing students gifted in the arts. Part of our mission is to provide an opportunity for students to pursue conservatory style training. Our state-of-the-art building at Lincoln Center was designed especially for the arts and features world-class facilities including a 1,150-seat concert hall, art, dance, music, recording and theater studios, and an art gallery.

At Mather, our Arts program in the classroom consists of Decorative Finishing in the Building Arts.  Decorative Arts introduces students to the materials and methods of historic architectural surface finishes, including decorative plaster, painted decorative finishes, and gilding.  Students receive hands-on instruction in the techniques of common historic finishes, as well as in their history, context, preservation, and present-day applications.  Units include Introduction to Paint, Color Theory and Application, Surface Preparation and Drawing/Transfer, Faux Finishes, Troweled Plaster Finishes and Gilding.

Outside of the classroom, our arts program consists of after school clubs including the performing/improv arts club, the musical club "The Matherizers," a singing group, and a visual arts club.

We also have offer summer opportunities for mural painting and craftsmship in carpentry.

Our Goals for the Arts Program remain the same as past years: It is our goal that all Lab students will be exposed to a variety of art experiences that will allow them to interact with art in a meaningful way and to cultivate a life-long relationship and appreciation for art. To nurture independent, creative thinking, the development of content knowledge, and a deeper appreciation of the visual arts, the art department uses a variety of instructional methods including the development of a studio-like environment, careful observation and writing about specific works of art, making inferences and interpretations, material explorations, class discussions, creative problem solving, the keeping of journals and sketchbooks, and the exposure of students to a wide variety of visual arts resources available in New York City. With regards to music, the curriculum is designed so that students can derive a meaningful learning experience regardless of prior knowledge and experience in music.

Art 1 This course is an introduction to the basic elements of art and principals of design. There is an emphasis on line, color theory, and composition used in two-dimensional art. This is a basic foundation course that will fulfill the graduation requirements recommended by the New York State Board of Regents. Students are exposed to a wide variety of studio experiences in drawing, painting, design and three-dimensional work. Art 2 This course is the second part of a one year sequence that satisfies the graduation requirements recommended by the New York State Board of Regents. This course is an introduction to art history, art criticism, aesthetics, and art production, with emphasis on the understanding and use of the elements and principles of design through a variety of media, processes, and visual resources. Students will do drawing, painting and sculpture to learn the ideas, language, and techniques of the visual artist. Students will study examples of work by well-known artists through slides and videos. Students will continue to develop art skills through a series of related assignments about the elements of art, the principles of composition, drawing techniques, color theory, art history, and criticism which will be evaluated to determine level of mastery. Drama Students will earned elective credit in drama and theater.

q44_1: This year our arts program included Visual Arts I and II, Theater I and II, Photography, and Portfolio Arts.  Our Theatre Arts teacher facilitated several successful community-building events, including two musicals and improv shows. All 9th grade students took a required visual arts course in which they acquired academic vocabulary for analyzing historic works of art, their peers' and their own art. They used a range of media, including mixed-media drawing/painting/collage, digital photography, and stop-motion animation to create visually and conceptually compelling works of art that fulfill aesthetic, expressive, narrative, and/or political art purposes. Students had the opportunity to engage in supplementary arts experiences through our after-school program, which includes Dance, Music and Comic Arts Clubs. Students participated in Animation and Film programs through BRIC arts residencies funded by the CASA grant. Our John Jay Campus hosted its second annual Sing program, through which students from all schools collaborated to write, choreograph and produce an original musical. We hope to be able to offer more rigorous arts electives moving forward in a greater range of media, including graphic design, music production, and film editing. Student photography was exhibited in a Gowanus Arts Studio, and at a coffee shop in Park Slope, and we will be showcasing senior art at a gallery in SoHo in June.

We have an in school arts residencies for each grade which included creative movement, collages, puppetry, self-portaits, and ballroom dancing. After school enrichment programs included African dance, contemporary dance, steel pan, violin, and band.

CS 211 believes strongly in the transformative effect that art has on children’s lives. As you walk through the halls of our school, you are greeted by beautiful student art. We offer a comprehensive visual arts curriculum Prek-8th grade. Students at CS 211 participate in a variety of performing arts residencies. Grades K-2 participate in an early childhood movement residency where students learn about music and dance. In the 3rd and 5th grades, students engage in Alvin Ailey& Flamenco workshops, Not only do the students learn the dance form but also go watch professional dance performances. In the 5th and 8th grades, students participate in a long in-depth ballroom dance residency culminating with a dance gala. Our dance team has won several dance awards. Our Bilingual students, take part in a musical theater residency. Students learn the music & dance from a current theater production and then create and perform their own original theater pieces. CS 211 middle school has an active marching band. The band practices often and participates in various parades in New York City and neighboring towns. CS 211 offers a free after-school art program for our Ell’s to increase language acquisition. CS 211 hosts several family art workshops for students and parents to learn together. CS 211 holds an annual visual art show representing all PreK-8 students. The art show is not only a display of exemplary work but also an opportunity for families to make art together.

CS 211 is a pre-K-8 school serving 622 students located in the Tremont section of the Bronx 60 % of our families live below the poverty level, and 70 % of families receive some form of public assistance.  Our student population is comprised of 27% English language learners and 24% Students with Disabilities. 

We hope to be able to increase our arts offering by adding another art teacher to our faculty next year.

q44_1: At the Isaac Clason School, we recognize the importance of integrating arts instruction into all curricular areas in order to motivate students to take greater ownership of their learning. Many of our students participate in our winter musical and our spring choral concert. This year, we continued to participate in Little Kids Rock program which donated instruments to play modern band music. We also were granted with CASA/ Inside Broadway which allowed many children to perform and learn from an artist-in-residence. It also provided the school two opportunities to visit Broadway.

Regarding performance arts, we run fifteen performance based music courses, including chorus, band, and orchestra. The students in our music courses compete in city-wide programs. Our arts courses include visual and digital arts. Our entire freshman class is enrolled in a visual arts/pre-engineering course. Mastery in the subject translates to college accreditation through Project Lead The Way at The Rochester Institute of Technology. Students perform one drama and one musical production in the auditorium for a large audience open to all each school year.

Our mission at the Earth School to support our students inherent love of learning through a curriculum that is engaging, playful, socially-conscious and rigorous. We are committed to knowing each student through his or her individual strengths and to nurturing the development of the whole child. To this end, students receive arts instruction that is integrated into the main curriculum of their classroom, as well as stand-alone arts instruction in visual arts, dance, music, and theater.

As a alternative transfer high school Arturo A. Schomburg Satellite Academy tries to provide as many academic and artistic opportunities for our students to meet their graduation requirements and become well rounded citizens in society. Though our funding may make it challenging to provide as much arts as we would like, we have been able to work with consultants and our teachers to provide art programs. This year we have been able to offer improvisational theater classes after school, Ceramics and visual art classes during the school day, and a dance program after school as well. It is our hope to continue these programs and add more opportunities depending on funding.

Grades K-3 artists learn art techniques and art history through a workshop model. Grades 4-8 artists are learning how to maneuver through a Choice-based art class. Our students take trips to several museums - MoMA, Whitney, Cloisters, the Rubin and the Met. This is the 4th year that our studio art teachers have created the school yearbook with 8th grade students. 
We have a rich music program with 2 full time music teachers. All students have music each week. K-2 learn general music using Solfege, and Orff instruments.  In grade 3 students learn the recorder. In fourth grade, all students learn an instrument for band. In grades 5-8 students have a choice of band or chorus.  8th graders also have a general music history class in which they also learn to compose using Garage Band and Finale. 
We partner with several organizations for drama. Our K students work with a teaching artist from the Creative Arts Team for interactive story telling. Students in grades 5-8 partner with Lincoln Center Education for theater workshops.  Fourth and fifth graders work with Kids Empowerment Academy on public speaking.

There are several goals that are incorporated into the arts program at P.S. 47: Goal 1-to provide a variety of art disciplines and create a continuum from k to 5 that will allow children to explore and discover their talents/ Goal 2-to develop a life-long love and appreciation for the arts/ Goal 3-to infuse the arts into all content areas, allowing teachers to provide differentiation based on individual student modalities and talents. P.S. 47 has adopted the Reggio Emelia philosophy which originated in Southern Italy. This philosophy is basically a "projects approach" to literacy and content area studies. Through the Reggio Emelia philosophy, children work cooperatively to develop art projects and culminating activities that include researching, writing and oral presentations. Goal 4-to align the arts with the New York State Standards for the Arts; creating and performing in the arts; knowing and using arts materials and resources; responding to and analyzing works of art.

FDR offers classes in disciplines including theatre, music, visual arts and film. Students can choose to sample various electives or major in a sequence. Yearly, FDR produces a play, musical, multicultural festival, talent show, and several concerts. Our school is involved with residency partnerships with the best cultural and arts organizations in New York, such as the TDF and Roundabout. Our art rooms include a ceramic studio and photography and computer art labs with state-of-the-art equipment for film and digital photography/restoration. Our music program has a concert band and guitar ensemble. The theatre department offers two tracks, performance or technical. FDR is starting a four year sequence which will end in a specialized arts-endorsed diploma. We are beginning work on a screened program. With its strong multicultural population, our Literacy Arts program helps ELL students improve language skills through artistic expression. Our goal in to instill a love and appreciation for the arts.

The current arts program at The Angelo Patri Middle School continues to expand.  We continue our work with Lincoln Center Shakespeare for our general education and special education students..  Broadway, Jr. is an integral part of our after school enrichment program and we have added band class this year.  DreamYard is continuing the work with our students around spoken word and will continue in the future looping with our current seventh grade students to eighth grade.  Our CBO, Replications, along with the Extended Learning Time staff engage our students in dance, visual arts, theater, and music.  Every student this year is touched by one form of the arts throughout the school year.  Our after school CBO, Eastside House provides media technology and music production to a group of students as well.  Students, teachers and families utilize the many cultural organizations throughout New York.  Some of these organizations include Bronx Museum of the Arts, MOMA, The Met, The Reuben Museum and the Cooper Hewitt Museum.

Our art appreciation program addresses the arts standards aligned with New York State performance indicators. Units of study are developed and implemented using the Department of Education's Blueprints. Classroom teachers focus on providing a well-balanced art program using a variety of media. This program enhances content area initiatives, especially in the reading and writing programs, through grade level unit planning. A music teacher supports both vocal and instrumental music programs for all students. The art teacher provides both art history and visual art programs for all students. Art, dance and music clubs provide enrichment opportunities for our students. Theater programs allow students to express themselves in the form of drama in their classrooms and in monthly assemblies. Readers Theater enhances our literacy curriculum.

At The George V. Brower School we believe that all students are uniquely gifted.  Our core belief has led us to engage students in multifaceted curricula that fosters creativity in drama and performing and visual arts.  We work collaboratively with parents, community organizations and faculty members to design rich and engaging learning opportunities in music, art, drama and dance.  Our teachers utilize the Blueprint for the Arts as a guide to create rigorous lessons that are intellectually challenging.

As a multi-cultural school with students from more than twenty counties, we construct projects that expose students to many cultures.   We believe that exposure to multi-culturalism will lead to respect and artistic appreciation of contributions other cultures have made to the global community.  Our school conducts cultural celebrations every semester.  Students create artistic presentations through visual art, music, dance and drama.

The George V. Brower administrative team and faculty members believe that engaging students in the arts promotes self-esteem and academic achievement.  Our interdisciplinary approach to teaching enables our students to analyze, synthesize and construct their own ideas and work products structured by content based learning.  Moreover, our instructional approach in the arts supports student learning with engagement through multiple learning styles.  Finally, all students regardless of disability or economic status have the opportunity to excel in the arts.

For the 2016-2017 school years we partnered with Notes in Motion providing dance instruction to identified students on grades two through five. Over the past ten years we have experienced great success through our partnership with Notes in Motion, each year the cooperating teachers and the dance instructors meet to determine the focus for the year, this allows the teaching artists to connect their lessons to an academic focus area. In addition, this year we have expanded the program to include a two part Parent and Child Workshop, where families can come in to watch a performance by the Amanda Selwyn Dancers and also to participate in a dance lesson where parents can learn about some of the things that their children have been experiencing. 

Our second partnership has been with Inside Broadway for a theater residency with identified fourth and fifth grade students. Here students are given the opportunity to create and perform in their very own musical. This residency helps to bolster our students’ confidence level as they perform for their audience.  Students and parents are excited about this wonderful opportunity and show their full support at our culminating performance. 

In addition, four of our students were awarded dance scholarships through Ballet Tech. This year, we hosted three seasonal performances and two performances for our dance and theater residencies. These performances provide our parents, teachers and students with an opportunity to watch our students as they showcase their talents and the skills.

The James Baldwin School infuses the arts into classes of many disciplines, like "Baldwin's Art and Soul." Although we have not had a school play this year, in all previous years our theater class has produced a school play, often one that is written by the students. In addition, we offer after school opportunities in the arts ranging from visual arts to spoken word. In addition, many of our students participate in programs in the arts with other organizations across the city (like the Possibilty Project, the MoMa, etc).

The Visual Arts program provides instruction to students in Pre K through grade five according to the Blueprint for the Arts. We provide residencies in dance and music instruction; extend learning beyond the classroom with museum visits,theater performances, and other venues that expose students to a life-long appreciation of the arts. PS 179 provides opportunities for parent engagement in the arts through student performances and annual art exhibit. PS 179 offers Chorus; Music Memory.After school programs include Art Club, Violin and Recorder instruction and Brooklyn Children's Theater after school program.
q45_1: PS 179 is a recipient of the Continuum Grant for Dance, and the ELL'S and SWD grant for Theater and Music. With our high ELL population, both these art forms have been a unique way for students to increase their language skills and explore new art forms. Our goal is to provide students with multiple opportunities to experience and appreciate the arts.

q44_1: Our school is dedicated to exposing students to the many opportunities New York City has to offer in the arts. Every semester we offer ballroom dancing through our physical education classes. Lincoln Center visits every semester to work with our students on a small theatrical performance. Our after school program allows students to explore museums across the city and attend Broadway shows. We offer choir, modern dance, drama and visual arts after school and they perform several times throughout the year. Our goal is to continue our partnerships and allow our students the opportunity to learn about American culture and living through the arts. Additionally we partner with Magic Box, Abrons Center for the Arts Henry Street Settlement, and Ballet Hispanico. From 2016 through 2020 we will be in a partnership with Exploring the Arts.

Our school continues to have a full time visual arts teacher who works weekly with all students in grades PK-5. All of our students receive additional arts education through extensive arts in school residencies in music, dance, and theater. Arts education is further supported through field trips.

This is PS 68's 19th year of collaboration with Education Through Music, Inc. ETM provides a teaching artist for our pull out string orchestra. The artist provides instruction twice weekly during and after school hours. Our grade 4 and grade 5 string orchestras are made up of approximately 50 students per grade who receive instruction on their string instrument of choice. Our music program is comprised of general music, recorder, violin, viola, cello, and bass. General music instruction is provided one to two times weekly for 50 minutes for Pre K-5th grades. We also have a grade 3-5 chorus that meets weekly after school. All students perform in at least one concert each semester as well as at festivals, presentations, and graduations. Additionally, after school services in music (drumming), dance (hip-hop), and the visual arts are provided by the Phipps Community Development Corporation, which provides instruction to 100 of our students.

The arts program at P.S. 65 has provided instruction aligned to the New York State Learning Standards for the Arts. This has included the following disciplines: visual arts, music, and theater arts. Our drama program is provided through an in-house after-school program. Our visual arts and music programs are provided through certified teachers on staff within the discipline.

Our arts program aims to give students exposure to dance and the visual arts through student interest-based concentrations. We aim for students to experience a multi-year program in the various genres of dance and diverse styles of visual arts. This includes experience through direct instruction in their concentration area, performance and observation in various venues. Students present their work three times per year during our Intersession Presentations. In addition, they create portfolios that showcase their development in their selected concentration area over three years.
q45_1: We have been part of the Arts Matter Program for visual arts over the past 3 years. We will exit that program next year and no longer receive program resources. Being part of the program has helped us to initiate our visual arts program, which students have excitedly participated in through scheduled classes and our after school art club. We have had students show their work in the Borough Arts Festival over the past 2 years. We intended to also offer dance instruction, but have been unable to hire a dance teacher. We would love to continue the program for dance and seek additional support in growing our arts program.

q44_1: At FHS, there is strong collaboration with Urban Arts Partnership. Academic teachers, a DOE certified visual art teacher and Urban Arts teaching artists co-plan curricula that integrate art, poetry, photography, music, and drama- all to deepen students’ understanding and provide multiple forms of expression in the classroom. The goals for the Arts Education Program are as follows: Provide all students with an inquiry-based, student-centered, and constructivist approach to arts learning; Provide all students with arts-integrated lessons and theme-based art studios. Our seniors participate in our annual Choosing to Participate exhibit which combines intense research on a social justice issue and the creation of an art activism piece displayed at the end of the year celebration. Our partnership has provided opportunity and access for all of our students both academically and artistically.

One of the biggest goals of the visual art program at our school is to make connections between the visual arts and other academic areas for interdisciplinary learning. In addition, we strive to give students the knowledge and skills they need to use art as a way to interpret and portray the world around them. We launched a music program this year. We provide sequential music instruction with students working towards music literacy. We have established a pattern of 2 concerts per term for students with additional opportunity for performances at special events and assemblies. This year we began beginning guitar instruction with a goal of working towards offering modern band instruction.
q45_1: We are on a cluster schedule. In this schedule, each student receives daily instruction in Art and in Music for approximately six weeks, one time per year (sometimes the duration of the cycle varies.) We also cycle with Math enrichment, Technology, Physical Education, and Science Enrichment. Six-week sessions present some advantages as well as some challenges. The learning curve is quite high for students receiving instruction on consecutive days; this schedule is conducive to project-based learning. Challenges include being able to track student progress over the duration of an entire school year.

q44_1: The school strives to provide high quality, comprehensive, sequential skills-based direct instruction to all K-5 students in the arts that enhances students' academic growth and general development. The school's arts programs address the five strands of arts learning: Arts Making; Literacy in the Arts; Making Connections; Community and Cultural Resources and Careers and Lifelong Learning. Instructional content is grade-specific and developmentally appropriate. The school has long lasting relationships with external arts organizations who help support the school's goal to provide students with a wide and deep arts education. Students are provided with multiple opportunities to perform and display their artistic talents for the school community during the school year.

Our goal is to provide our students with a range of arts courses. Our students are English language learners, thus the arts provide a medium of expression and language acquisition. The methods and strategies used to teach the arts support student learning.

Public School 105 continues to be dedicated to providing our students with exposure to a variety of disciplines in the Arts. We employ two full-time Music teachers, a full-time Drama teacher, and a full-time visual arts teacher. We also have a number of affiliations with outside organizations, such as: National Dance Institute, Bronx Dance Theater, Guggenheim Museum, Metropolitan Museum of Art, Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center. Additionally, members of the drama club, chorus and art club attend a yearly trip to Broadway, and have seen such shows as Stomp, Annie, Wicked, and this year, the Lion King. Specific highlights our Arts programs include: - Third Grade students participate in the Bronx Dance Theater working toward a culminating activity which is performed for our school community. - The National Dance Institute (NDI)provides themed expressive dance workshops for grade 4, also with a culminating activity/performance that takes place in June. - SWAT is an after school dance program offered through NDI, that provides dance enrichment for selected students of various grade levels. - The school chorus and band, under the direction of our Music teacher performs both on and off site concerts throughout the year. This year the chorus has performed at Riker's Island, the Bronx VA Hospital and various tree lighting ceremonies throughout the Bronx. - The school drama performs various shows throughout the year for our school community. - The school Art club creates the setting and backdrops for our school performances.
Students in grades 9-12 receive visual arts instruction in Required Art and Painting courses.

Through a partnership with the New York City WEB Center students learn how to write and record music in our recording studio and the skills associated with television production in our television production studio.

Over their three years in middle school at LMC our goal is to provide students with a basic orientation of multiple art forms and establish deeper facility and competence in a single art form of their choosing. As 6th graders our students participate in an arts wheel through which they take 8 weeks of instruction in each of the following art forms: dance, music, digital arts, and visual arts. At the conclusion of their 6th grade year, students participate in a series of auditions and select one of these art forms in which they will specialize over the next two years. Through their three years of middle school our students have multiple opportunities to showcase their art work. 6th graders demonstrate their work four times through the year during morning art exhibitions that are open to families. Our 7th and 8th graders share their work twice a year in evening art showcase and performance exhibitions. In all three years of our arts program students perform multiple times for peers, the school community and the public. Performance is a skill and experience that we believe to be a key component of arts instruction in our school.

The Laboratory School of Finance and Technology provides quality arts instruction for all of our student body. We expose our students to at least three art disciplines: orchestra and band for 6th grade, theater for 7th grade and visual art or dance for 8th grade. Our teachers continually strive to reinforce literacy skills as well as a true appreciation for the arts. We believe that the arts create a path to expression that might not have been an option to every student in our community. To create greater pride in their work, we have art celebrations, such as gallery showings, and culminating performances in music, dance and theater. We are proud to put on an annual production through Broadway Jr. and offer arts programming during expanded day and the summer. We also go out to attend performances and bring in performers to create young consumers of art.
q45_1: We have an extensive summer program that is privately funded that is based on the arts.  Each student gets four hours of arts for 100 hours which is more than most schools provide in a year.  Music, dance, theater, visual arts, and media are all represented.  And we love our support from the DOE!

q44_1: Our program consist of a full-time full time visual arts teacher. A separate room is dedicated to the art program.The goal of our school is to provide each student access to the program as required by NYSDOE/NYCDOE

P.S. 51 currently offers a well-rounded, standards-driven arts program that combines the elements of visual art, music, movement, dance, and theater to enhance the overall educational experience of our students. Through extensive horizontal and vertical collaboration among arts and classroom teachers, students are provided with multiple opportunities to share their skills and creative talents with the entire school community through arts shows, instrumental and vocal concerts, and dance performances. Our arts teachers have designed a unique program including special clubs and classes like fashion design, Chorus, Orff Ensemble, Recorder Ensembles, guitar and ukulele classes, violin and cello classes, and music theater in addition to the scaffolded curriculum offered in weekly arts classes. We strive to provide a safe and nurturing environment where students are encouraged to transcend emotional boundaries and explore their creative energies.
q45_1: Our music and art teachers taught weekly dance classes to all of our PreK and Kindergarten classes this school year.

q44_1: In the 2016-17 school year we were able to increase our arts program through a NYC DOE grant that provided a music residency program through Creative Music Programs-Seth Ginsberg for approx. 12 weeks for students in every grade.  Our dance/theatre program continues as a full time cluster position and there is a Dance Theater Workshop program on Friday afternoons and Saturday mornings.  Through CASA grant funding from the City Council, we are able to provide additional visual arts programs on Friday afternoons and Saturday with instruction provided by Studio in a School. We will continue our partnership with the NY Historical Society to provide arts based residencies for all classes PreK - Grade 5.

At PS 340 we encourage and support arts education in numerous ways. We employ a full time music teacher who provides music and keyboard instruction through the Music and the Brain program to students in pre-k to 2nd grade. We have a full time Dance teacher who provides dance instruction in our large dance studio to all of the children in our school. pre-k to 2nd grade. Our kindergarten and 1st/2nd grade students receive visual arts instruction from our in-house, part-time art teacher, and pre-k students receive art instruction from their classroom teachers. We have a partnership with the Joyce Theater that involves a residency and visits to a dance performance. Take Two film company works with our 2nd grader in a 10 week residency program in our school to create documentaries. Learning by Design, an architecture company, provides a 10 week program for our kindergarteners. Additionally, we regularly go on visits to museums (Whitney and the Rubin), and offer art instruction within the regular classroom.

Our arts program follows the New York City blueprint which is grounded in the national and New York State learning strands. These strands guide teachers in addressing specific learning goals for students. They also provide the guidelines for offering a diverse visual art, dance and musical experience. The visual arts program is structured around the Art Making strand of the blueprint. Our artists are given the opportunity to work in different media, including painting, drawing, collage,sculpture and printmaking. Our music program provides our students with many opportunities to express themselves through music. Students in grade 4-8 have the opportunity to participate in the school band or chorus program

All students at Bronx Community High School are required to take two arts classes during the course of their high school education to graduate. The courses focus on the NYC Standards, the Blueprint for the Arts and CCLS. In the Visual Arts, these include art making, the historical/cultural context of the arts, literacy in the arts and career and lifelong learning in the arts. There is an emphasis on art making and the exploration of materials in each class. During class students work towards mastery of media and a strong conceptual base for the value of arts in education and as a vehicle for student voice in a community. In Dance, these courses include dance making, developing dance literacy, making connections, working with community and cultural resources, and exploring careers and lifelong learning. Several times per year students are provided the opportunity to visit cultural organizations around the city and, when possible, outside artists/professionals are brought in to classes to teach and discuss about careers in the arts. We offer our students a variety of courses such as Urban Art, Design it Yourself (DIY), Printmaking, 3-Design, Art & Design, Art for Change, etc.

We have revised our plan to expand the Arts Education in the Shakespeare School. To realize the plan’s goals, each teacher was  asked to incorporate the arts into their day-to-day culture. This shift spans five years and is divided into two achievable phases, although access to the arts will be evident immediately. Equitable arts opportunities for students will be realized increasingly, as the culture of the Shakespeare School is strengthened and supported school wide.  
This strategic plan is based on a continuum for implementation , with an emphasis in three focus areas that are essential to its success. Its projected outcomes hope to spark policy, future action plans and budget recommendations for implementing a sequential and standards - based curriculum in the arts outlined at every grade level (not only 2nd and 5th as identified in the Blueprint for the Arts).   
This process has fostered further community awareness and hopes to provide the structure and catalyst for sustainable relationships between the Shakespeare School and key arts stakeholders. This concept is founded in the idea that every member of the community has an important piece of the larger puzzle, offering valuable resources that will contribute to the greater good - the future art education, awareness and experience of the scholars at the Shakespeare School!
q45_1: We continue to produce Disney Musical in Schools production, absorbing full costs of the program. We chose to invest in sustaining the Musicals in our school because of the profound impact it has with all of our students, especially our English Language Learners and Students with Disabilities. This year we selected The Little Mermaid Jr. A musical that is normally conducted at the middle school level. Our directors took on the challenge to provide our students with more enrichment time and activity with the arts. We continue to employ Dimitri Saari of The Society of the Educational Arts liaison to help design and build our set from recyclable materials.  Our students are dedicated, talented and professional, and this is a direct reflection of the commitment our teachers have toward exposing our students to multiple facets of arts instruction through theater.

q44_1: P.S. 268's art program is designed to support our students' creative ways of thinking  and provides them with numerous opportunities to express themselves artistically. We continuously strive to make sure that our instructional art program is aligned with the  Common Core art standards and grade benchmarks as outlined in the Blue Print for visual arts.

Students of Mott Hall Community School are exposed to both Visual Arts and Instrumental Music as part of their weekly schedule. Most classes have art twice a week, and music twice a week. The courses focus on the NYC standards for the art, blueprint arts, and the Common Core Learning Standards. These include art and music making, literacy in the arts and careers and lifelong learning in the arts. Several times a year students visit cultural institutions and go on hands-on trips to broaden their culture in the arts. Student work is exhibited throughout the school year, and there are several musical performances each year, including talent shows, and performances for "Little Kids Rock." Students are taken on trips to visit arts high schools in seventh grade and are encouraged to audition form arts high schools. This year 2016-2017, 4 of our students made Arts High Schools. Our Exposure after school program meets daily from 3-6 pm and provides art enrichment to those who join. They work with film editing, music producing, dance, theater, graphic design, and visual arts as well.

P.S 185 Early Childhood Discovery and Design Magnet School (ECDD) is committed to providing a high quality arts education to every student. We provide our students with vocal music, piano keyboard, Orff, dance, and visual arts instruction as part of the regular curriculum. In addition, we partner with community arts organizations to expose children to a wide range of performance and visual arts. At ECDD, a strong foundation in arts literacy prepares our students for a lifetime of arts appreciation as well as providing them with rich contexts for problem solving, creativity, collaboration and communication of thoughts and ideas.

PS/MS 20 has a junior chorus for students interested in learning performance and vocal techniques. The students will exhibit these techniques in concerts. Additionally, interested students will have the opportunity to learn how to use instruments such as violin, recorder, xylophone and keyboard. Early elementary students will learn and experience playing percussion instruments and keyboard. Additionally, the school will seek out Cultural Arts Organizations to identify programs that can be brought to students in school.

q42_r1_c1: Learning through an Expanded Arts Program
q44_1:
Health Opportunities High School provides students with the opportunity to take dance and art elective classes in their regular schedule. Theater is incorporated in the English classes and is taught by a LEAP guest artist teacher with rehearsals done after school. Students write and produce ten minutes plays and ten plays are selected and produce in school while the first place play is performed on Broadway where students as well as parents are given the opportunity to watch these performances. Liberty Partnership, a community based organization, works with the school to provide our students with the opportunity to participate in Digital Photography, Art Therapy and band.Students work are presented at an Art Exhibition at Hostos Community College as well as in our school's lobby area. 

Students have the opportunity to participate in music by joining the school choir who sings at school functions as well as off site functions.Each year the school hosts its annual fashion, talent and lip sync shows, which have students participating in modeling, dancing,poetry, drama and music. This year students had the opportunity to participate in fashion textile by creating and designing different outfits and accessories such as handbags , hats etc. Students participated in patchwork creation, embroidery, knitting, painting, drawing and designing. We are committed to developing students academically and giving them a solid foundation in art education which will prepare them for college and career and creating a well rounded individual.
q45_1:
Our students are not expose to the arts in their home environment. Therefore it is our responsibility to provide them with the opportunity to experience the different forms of art and to encourage,  promote and foster a healthy art culture for our students. 

We do not have sufficient funds to provide a comprehensive art experience for our students. We would appreciate special funding that is designated only for the arts. However, we do try to provide art exposure for our students with the budget that we are given annually.

q44_1: At PS23 we are committed to providing our students access to a wide variety of arts programming. This year we focused on dance, theater and visual arts. Through a grant through from the Walentas Foundation we were able to provide all students in pre-K kindergarten first grade and every single special education class the opportunity to learn dance. Students in second and third grade were engaged in a music series and students in fourth and fifth grade learned engineering through the use of digital design. This partnership was with the 92nd St. Y and supported our vision to provide students with STEAM education. Furthermore, we were able to partner with BRI C where students in second and third grade were involved in visual arts and students in fourth and fifth grade learned videography and made a short film. Finally, students in grades two through five were involved in a guitar club which took place after school. Our arts classroom is equipped to provide visual art instruction to all classes. It is our goal to continue these programs obviously pending the funding.

Our goal is to continue to expose our students to different art forms. Since we do not have a full time Art teacher, so we brought in several art residencies from Marquis Studio and Music for Many to work with our k-5th grade students. The Residency with Marquis Studio was funded by Council Member of the 40th district, Matthew Eugene. This program funded an after-school art program for our 1at and 2nd grade students.  Music for Many provide residencies foo grade k-5 in Music, Dance and arts.

At The Arthur Tappan School - PS/MS 46, we believe that Arts education helps to form the basis of a well-rounded student. We continue to foster partnerships, with recognized art institutions, to build an appreciation for the different media, in addition to hiring and retaining art educators who bring the disciplines to life for our students. Through the Arts, we hope to foster in our students an appreciation for the varied forms.

The Arts program at Bronx Theatre High School provides students with a well-rounded exposure to various forms of the arts. Students at Bronx Theatre High School are encouraged early on to work with each other as an ensemble, and this is conveyed through various forms of artistic expression such as performance, set & costume design and visual arts. As students progress through grade levels, they are given numerous opportunities to work with content teachers and Roundabout Theatre Teaching Artists to explore various aspects of the arts including set design, costume design, dance and acting. Students who express interest in dance work with our in-house Dance Company and choreograph performances.  All graduating seniors have the opportunity to "walk" on a Roundabout Theatre Broadway stage. Advanced, and dedicated thespians, who earn 10 or more art/theatre credits (including Advanced Placement Studio Art & Photography/Videography) are eligible to sit for the Comprehensive Theatre Regents examination in their senior year - they have an opportunity for an Arts Endorsed Regents upon graduation. Roundabout Theatre Company has been our partnering organization since the opening of the school in 2003 and continues to provide services to our students through in-class residencies and pre/post-show workshops. Studio art and Advanced Placement Studio Art are new offering at the school in which students complete a sequence of coursework and generate a portfolio of various works including Pop Art, Abstract Drip Art and multi-media collage.

This school year we were fortunate to have Inside Broadway and Inside Voices where the artists worked with our fourth and fifth grade students as they created a play on immigration and wrote their screen plays.

In addition, students in grades kindergarten through fifth received art classes with an intern from TC throughout the school year.

Our four Pre K classes enjoyed a small Studio in the school grant for three months where the teachers received profession development and an artist worked with the teachers and students.

BAHS works with a variety of educational consultants to provide students with access to a myriad of art forms: dancing, singing and acting. Art programs are created based on student interest during and after the school day. Art programs are designed to include all learners through the lens of character development.

Kingsbridge International High School has an expanding arts program, including a new ceramics program. With two brand new kilns, students are able to create works of art using ceramics as a medium, using their knowledge of proportion, three-dimensions, and color.

Thaddeus Stevens PS 81 supports the arts because it improves individual well-being, unifies communities, improves academic performance, sparks creativity and innovation and helps keep children in school. With these reasons in mind, we collaborate with Community Based Organizations to help us finance our Arts program.  One of our biggest supporters in "Change For Kids".  This organization (CBO) has brought visual art residency, theater residency to our scholars, teachers and parents.  As a result of this collaboration, our students are more confident when making their thinking visible in and outside of the classroom. Through the work of another community based organization, "Inspire Corp", Yoga, African dance, song writing and visuals arts are also offered to students based on their choice.  We would love to have a residency that supports theatre.  However, teachers use literacy periods to incorporate the art of speaking and acting. We are a Title 1 school in good standing.  Many of our  students come from shelters, single family homes or foster care.  Nevertheless, we understand that access and exposure can make a difference in the lives of all students.  With this in mind, we are determined, that budgetary constraints will not hinder our students from receiving 21st century skills that support learning in other core subjects, "The Arts".

All students take a full year (2 credits) of visual arts in 10th grade, where they explore different mediums, including collage, drawing, painting and murals. They study contemporary artists and explore the issues of identity and self. Students have the option to apply for Honors Art in 11th and 12th grade, where they develop a portfolio for post-secondary arts programs. With a partnership with Manhattan Class Company Theater, students explore drama integrated into all English classes, from grades 9-12, with reinterpretations of Shakespeare, spoken word poetry, dramatic interpretation of American novels, and rhetoric. There is also an after school drama program, which puts on our annual school play. We have a partnership with American Composers Orchestra, who works with 9th grade English classes to examine tone and music. There is an after school rock music club and an after school dance club.
We continue to participate in the Noel Pointer Violin Program, Disney Musical in Schools and we have our own Woodshop Program.

We are strongly committed to the arts and will work to strengthen the arts at our school for all students in grades pre-kindergarten to 8th grade. We intend to build upon existing partnerships such as LEAP, Music Kafando, and Thrive Collective to fulfill our goal of meeting the creative needs of all students.

At the Fresh Creek School we believe in educating the whole child. At the heart of this philosophy is a commitment to providing all of our students with opportunities to develop their many intelligences.To that end we provide instruction in music and arts to every child. We have expanded our string program to include not only violin, but cello as well. We offer instruction as an elective during the day and an after school component. We have caipoeria instruction as well as African dance and drumming classes for after school with clinics for visual arts and music appreciation. for our early childhood we have puppetry to develop their theater skills

Our arts programs have been designed to create an arts culture in our school where every child receives the opportunity to express themselves, both artistically and socially, through all subjects, including the arts. Our aim is to work with the resources (time, personnel, and money) our school possesses so that we may give our students the best possible arts education with the end goal of enriching our students lives and their artistic and academic futures

We offer students a full compliment of Visual Arts and through partnerships with Community based Organizations are able to offer decorative Arts as well. We strive to provide opportunities in web design and audio engineering.

The Museum School offers a 4-year studio art sequence aligned with the New York State Blueprint for the Arts standards. All art courses are interdisciplinary and taught by a fully licensed and certified art teacher. Unique to our school are the "museum module" courses, which allow students to take specialized museum-based courses every week that correlate with in-school Regents-based courses. Our goal is to provide students with as rich an arts education as possible while reinforcing the connections between the arts and the core disciplines. Students frequently visit the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Japan Society, the Rubin Museum, the Museum of Natural History, the Paley Center for Media, and more! The arts are a highly valued part of the Museum School experience.

The Clinton Hill School strives to provide each student with an arts education that will develop creative ability and nurture a life long appreciation for the various art forms. Teachers engage students in project based educational experiences that integrate the arts across all subject areas and disciplines while addressing the academic and social needs of our diverse student population. Through our partnerships with many cultural organizations, the students are exposed to a variety of art forms, artists and techniques. These various art forms help students develop motor skills, gain exposure to music/theatre using imagination, learning audience skills, movement skills and cooperation. Students showcase their art through concerts, performances, galleries and displays in local businesses.

Students are enrolled in a dance course to earn credits towards graduation. Our students are required to earn either two art or two music credits towards graduation. Each semester this year students are eligible to enroll in a dance class where they earn one or a half credit per semester. The pedagogue grades them on assignment completion and also on the students' portfolios being gathered all semester. Students also may participate in 'YRAP: Youth Recording Apprenticeship Program' afterschool music program. During this program, students write, produce and record songs.

Our school provides integrated instruction to students in all grades. Therefore, the students are required to create art projects that are aligned to their units of study. All 4-6 week long units include two project based homework assignments that include some form of art. Additionally, our Art teacher aligns the art instruction to the units being studied in class. All projects are assessed through the use of rubrics. They are also provided with constructive feedback from their peers and teachers. Student work and efforts are acknowledged at the end of every school year by hosting an art gala. Families and local community members are invited to enjoy the beautiful artwork.

At River East, we provide a comprehensive arts education program. We partner with several community based organizations to enhance student opportunities in the arts. With this support, we are able to offer full time visual arts instruction, pottery, violin, dance, and chorus as well as a music program in which students participate in a series of interactive concerts that introduce music from various parts of the world.

P.S. 249 strives to enrich student learning by aligning the arts curriculum with the Common Core Learning Standards, supporting student independence, content knowledge and the ability to think and speak critically. The young artists at P.S. 249 are encouraged to engage fully in the art-making process, taking creative risks and developing their own voices. Throughout the school year, students have multiple opportunities to display and perform their work as well as share in artful experiences with their families and community. The Arts Teacher Team continues to work collaboratively to make sure lessons are supported by the NYC Blueprints for the Arts and to stand behind the mission of P.S. 249 which is to nurture students as they become college and career ready.

Our school's arts program is comprised of in-house initiatives in which music and theater are incorporated into the daily instructional program by arts cluster teachers and music and movement by a non-arts cluster teacher. This year we have a licensed music teacher and theater arts teacher. In addition, we contract consultants such as Dancing in the Classroom. This year we will continue to participate in a grant with the Salvation Army that allows us to foster the love of music by having the children play in an orchestra. Extended day programs in music and visual arts are provided through after school enrichment clubs and arts programs in which students receive instruction in playing the clarinet and drama. We have a variety of clubs in drama, dance, and music taught by in-house staff. Our students have participated in city-wide dance competitions and have won second place for the various genres of ballroom dances. As a school we have a strong commitment and vision for the arts.

Our goal at PS/MS 96 is to provide our students with a complete and comprehensive Arts Program for next year. This will be enriching to our current curriculum via our teachers and also be supported by many cultural organizations which will partner with us in the future. Our goal for next year is to include 3 Arts Disciplines; Visual Arts, Dance and Music as well as continuing to provide Technology. Our students will work with their art teachers who will align projects to their core subjects, as well as promoting art outcomes including shows, digital displays, concerts and performances for our greater community. We also look forward to offering Arts Workshops for parents and their children broadening our scope as a community school. Through the connection to the arts we look ahead to positive and tangible improvements in learning across all educational disciplines.  We also hope to provide our Middle school students can connect arts to relevant cultural and career opportunities.  Our Middle school students will have opportunities for portfolio specials going forward into the new year.

We provide music instruction through the Noel Pointer Strings Program. We have also partnered with LEAP, Neighborhood Music and Arts, and the Brooklyn Arts Council to provide visual media and the arts to our literacy instruction. Students view and participate in monthly assembly programs written and produced by the teachers. Students in music programs participate in musical concerts as well. We have a parent volunteer who provides classroom art instruction to students in grades K-5. Art sales/exhibits were held three times this year.

At the Manhattan School for Children, we believe that the arts are vital to our children's education, and that the exploration of the arts nurtures their creativity, imagination and ability to see other points of view as they make personal connections to the world they live in. To foster this vision, the school community has developed a dynamic and well-organized arts program across arts disciplines that is inclusive of our children's backgrounds and of the world's cultures. We are committed to a vision of the school as a community of learners, who are empowered to create their work and share their process. We achieve this vision by the integration of the arts experiences within classroom curriculum and the broad exposure to the arts through our collaborations with neighborhood cultural institutions. Our school is currently in a vertical grade research project with Lincoln Center Institute with the goal of understanding how to implement the capacities for imaginative learning across cohorts. In addition, we have embarked making our vision for an MSC Music Department a reality with an all-school sequential music program and have hired a music director for our MSC chorus classes and a percussion teacher. We have also added four music electives to our elective roster: Band, Percussion, Chorus and MSC Glee

Fostering our students’ creativity and talent is a part of P.S./I.S. 163's mission statement and a major component of our students' education. 

In addition to regularly scheduled music classes, our school has a chorus, a guitar club, a band, and an orchestra. The students who are members of these groups, as well as many others, participate in and perform in our Winter Concert and our Spring Arts Festival. Our Dance program exposes students to various types of dance, classical and contemporary, and presents them with the opportunity to express themselves through movement. Our Visual Arts program provides students in grades K-8 a well-rounded visual arts experience that covers both art history and hands on art projects. 

At P.S./I.S. 163, the arts are an integral part of student learning, as they help students to make connections between subjects and gain a sense of pride and accomplishment by recognizing their creative talents and potential.

We offer students a choice of arts electives 3-4 times per week. This year’s arts elective class choices are visual arts and music/theater. Our visual arts class is taught by a full-time arts certified teacher and our music/theater class is taught by a full-time music teacher. We continue to utilize Musica De Camera as one of the finest arts organizations NYC has in classical music. We have increased student involvement in music through a partnership with Musica De Camara teaching violin to our students after school. Our music program is budding every year with performances showcasing the best MS 127 has to offer. Our partnership with our after school program, Sports and Arts in Schools continues to further offer students with additional instruction and exposure in the arts. Some classes offered this year include African drumming, vocal music, piano, step, Hip-Hop dance, water color painting, sculpture and sewing.

q45_1: The Eagle Academy for Young men (09x231) is an all male school in the Bronx. The school is grades 6-12 and has 522 young men. We have many diverse scholars and aim to ensure they are expressing their cultural pride through the arts.

q44_1: The arts program at Dual Language Middle School focuses upon developing students’ literacy in the visual and performing arts. Within the three-year sequence of studio arts classes students participate in the process of art-making through the exploration of artistic history and the various media, subject matter, and symbolism therein. Students respond critically to a variety of works in the arts and make connections between the art and other subjects as a result of their studies. Students develop understanding of and appreciation for the reasons people and cultures construct works of art, both visual and performance, and how the arts shape the diverse cultures of past and present society. During the three-year dance sequence, students explore not only the steps, but also the history and symbolism within dances from a variety of cultures and time periods including Bharatanatyam, traditional African dance, Salsa, Hip-Hop, Jazz, and ballroom dance styles to name a few.

We believe that the arts play a vital role in helping to improve our students' academic performance and achievement by providing a variety of venues for them to develop the necessary language and social skills, self-confidence and poise needed to succeed. Students enjoy coming to school so our attendance rate is among the highest in the city. Our comprehensive program includes our in-house music and art programs and an arts residency program for every child from Pre-K through Grade 5. Many of our arts partnership programs offer scholarships to students who show a particular interest or talent in a discipline and also provide opportunities for them to continue after they leave PS 130. In addition to our day school offerings, we also have many free school-sponsored after school programs such as a competitive fife and drum corps, a school chorus, a ballroom dance club, and a Chinese lion dance club. Parents actively support our many programs by volunteering and raising funds to pay for partnerships with Community Based Organizations, musical instruments, and equipment.
q45_1: All of the arts programs listed in the survey have been made possible by the generosity of our parents and our Parents Association. We are a Title I school with a majority of children coming from homes that speak a language other than English. Because the parents see the value and the positive impact that the arts have had on their children's academic performance, they have been tremendously supportive in helping us to raise the funds necessary to continue the programs. As a result, our school has consistently ranked as one of the higher performing schools in New York City.

q44_1: PS 119 is committed to developing the whole child with a focus on the arts. Students are given art and music instruction from PreK through grade 5. A magnet school, each year students study diverse cultures with a culminating Expo demonstrating student learning and achievement.  An important part of the school culture is to expose our children to global traditions while promoting peace on earth.   Art is seen as a tool for creative expression as well as a pathway for language development and behavior modification.  Our arts partners work in concert with the arts educators and classroom teachers to provide the most coherent scaffolding of lessons for making meaning through the arts.  Students annually visit performances through out the year at Brooklyn College including dance, theater and storytelling. It is through this far reaching arts approach that we believe children are motivated to enjoy learning across the curriculum as they evolve into their best selves.

Arts is a vehicle for expression of ideas that serves to enhance educational, academic, and social experience of children at the school. Children benefit from regular and structured arts programs, each and every day. Art develops intelligence, competencies, and skills that have a direct link to academic performance. Our goal is to allow students to experience a rich and diverse arts program. As we grow to scale, we envision regular participation in all art disciplines for all students. Currently, we have a full time visual arts provider to deliver art lessons in school. Theater skills are incorporated in our SELF (Social Emotional Learning Foundation) program. Students also have opportunities to visit cultural organizations and arts venues on school trips to experience the arts outside of school. In addition, we currently have a partnership Creative Music Program to ensure our students receive music instruction, and we will continue this partnership next school year. Our third graders are working with a teaching artist to create a permanent installation in our school building. To enrich the lives of our families, we worked with Center for Arts Education to provide two family programs. We had an after school puppetry program and a dance program for parents and children. During their middle school years scholars will have a host of opportunities in the Arts.  All sixth graders will receive a full year of Visual Arts and will work with such outside partners as LeAp and Lincoln Center.
