C.S. 67's arts program consists of instruction within both the arts classroom and all general education classrooms. We strive to incorporate the arts into daily lesson plans through the use of "move to improve" and "visual thinking strategies". Within the visual arts classroom, scholars engage in painting, sculpting, drawing, print-making and explore various tools, mediums and techniques. Scholars have gained knowledge on different artists, analyzed various forms of artwork and cultural differences through the history of art. Scholars are encouraged to reflect on their own artwork and provide peer feedback through the use of rubrics and checklists. Teachers also provide specific feedback through a "glow", "grow" and "how to" which is collected in their art portfolios. q44_1: Our school offers a challenging arts program to students in grades 6-12. Students in all grades receive the opportunity for arts instruction in instrumental music, Theater Arts, Animation and/or Visual Arts. Students in grades 6 and 7 take one semester of each arts course before settling on an area of focus for 8th grade to expose them to all of the art forms. High School students are provided with a choice regarding their arts program and are able to choose from a variety of disciplines.  Within their major, students dive deep into different forms of coursework and are expected to be a part of our school's performances, concerts, gallery exhibitions, and arts-based internships. Partnerships with BRIC, NYU Steinhardt, Little Kids Rock and NURTUREart provide students with professional arts opportunities.

UA Maker offers courses in Theater and Visual Art where students will engage in both making and critical thinking. The first unit of Visual Art, “Art Begins With a Mystery", provides students with experiences uncovering and expressing ideas through visual imagery. In Theater, students begin by learning about storytelling, uncovering the deep connections between design thinking and artistic creativity. Visual Art offers students the opportunity to develop strategies and techniques for making 2D visual art; including proficiency with line and weight, shape and form, value, color, and perspective. In the later half of the class students will practice and refine these skills in independent works, and explore the social and historical context of various artistic expressions. Theater encourages students to extend their expressive and interpersonal skills, building their work in other classes by developing their confidence and comfort presenting to an audience of their peers. Throughout the latter half of the class, students will explore more sophisticated areas of performance, with options ranging from clowning and comedy to the writing, performance, and analysis of Hip Hop poetry. Students will engage with art and art making both in and out of the classroom. They will be expected to produce exhibitions of their own work as well as portfolios of their growth. They will engage artists, art makers, and art spaces in public and community settings in order to explore careers in the arts.

Our goal at Public School 250 is to continue to have a comprehensive arts education program that is interdisciplinary and aligned to the Blueprint for the Arts. Our Magnet theme of Communications and Multimedia Arts will continue to be embedded throughout the school curriculum. We recognize the importance that the arts plays in developing students who are creative, critical thinkers and students who can solve real world problems in order to express themselves in different ways. At PS 250, the arts disciplines are incorporated into the school curriculum as a means to encourage cultural sensitivity diversity, and community involvement.  We pride ourselves in keeping the arts at the forefront of our students' educational experiences.

The goal of PS99 is to raise achievement levels for all students in PreK-8 through the integration of a rigorous standards based arts program. We incorporate the NYC Blueprint for Teaching and Learning in the the Arts into all curricula areas. Students will develop the skills needed to meet or exceed benchmarks. Students perform in plays and choral presentations in school and at charitable organizations. The community at large is invited and encouraged to be involved. All of our 7th and 8th Grade students meet the required number of instructional hours needed for Graduation in the Arts.

Foundation classes in visual art are offered to grades K through 5. The visual arts curriculum is aligned to the NYC Blueprint for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. Through exploration of painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, sculpture, 2D-design students develop an understanding of the Elements of Art & the Principles of Design and the 5 strands of Arts Learning. We also offer learning through theater arts programing connecting historical and cultural concepts covered in the classroom and expressed through performance. In addition, we offer specialized Violin and Recorder instruction to our kindergarten and 1st grade students. Our 3rd, 4th and 5th grade students travel within the community to take Ballet and Hip Hop dance classes in partnership with the Cynthia King Dance Studio.  Further investigations of dance, theater arts performances, art and design exploration are incorporated throughout the P.S. 6 Arts philosophy. Our goal is to continue to grow the P.S. 6 arts program each year adding by another discipline in order to deepen the imaginative and creative capacities of our students.  Our goal is to educate the whole child; the arts are a large contributor to this philosophy.

As a school exclusively for newcomer English language learners, our goal is to provide all students with an equal opportunity to access the
arts. Therefore, all of our students take drama in grades 9-10, and visual art in grades 9-11. Each year, students participate in the creation, display, and critique of their art work. q45_1: While our high school is one of NYC’s many public high schools that are operated under the NYC DOE, we remain a unique and specialized school who caters to teaching a student body made entirely of English language learners. Our students come from over 40 different countries, speak over 20 different home languages, and practice a variety of religious faiths. 88% of our students are eligible for free school meals, 60% are overage for their grade level, and 35% are Students with Interrupted Formal Education (SIFE), who by definition have had gaps of two or more years in formal schooling. In addition to coming to us from all corners of the world, our students commute from all five boroughs to our school.

q44_1: The Brooklyn Brownstone School offers both music and visual art to all of its students, two to three times a week. The goals of our arts program promotes serious artistic study, while also making inter-disciplinary connections to core subjects. We have aligned our instructional goals with the Common Core Standards and the Blueprint for the Arts. Art education includes working with various kinds of materials, art history, and an after school art club fro qualified students.  The music program includes choral music, music history, music theory and instrumental music. We participate in Little Kids Rock, creating student bands, giving meaningful experience to careers in music and team building. We participate in Music in the Brain for Pre-K to 2nd grade,learning how to play keyboard, music theory for beginners,experiencing variety of musical styles, composing and improvising. Opportunities to see students artistic talent are available throughout the year. Student art is continually posted on the walls of our school. We host art exhibitions and visit NYC galleries as well as participate in art exhibitions held in our district. There are two in-school music performances during the year, as well as monthly musical performances aligned with our character building curriculum "Heartwood". Musicians and artists visit from the community to provide instruction and information about careers in music. All projects and activities reinforce our commitment to produce critical thinkers and life-long learners.

The mission of PPAS is to provide professional performing arts instruction to all students in grades 6 – 12 in a variety of disciplines, while also providing them with a rigorous academic curriculum that will lead to exceptional higher education choices that include, but are not limited to, top performing arts colleges and conservatories. The performing arts curriculum offers students in grades six through twelve a unique opportunity to study the arts in a professional environment. Professional artists offer training to meet the performing arts learning needs of students who are passionate about the arts and committed to the study of the arts. High School students major in professional studios in dance, drama, musical theater, and vocal music. Middle School students participate in a variety of performing arts classes to increase their exposure to performance elements. These classes include acting, dance, singing and music appreciation. PPAS has a unique programming structure where the school partners with professional arts organizations that provide top quality instruction in professional settings. Student take classes in site-specific high caliber studios, which include off-Broadway theaters, concert halls, and ballet and tap dance studios. Students present concerts, plays, and other productions throughout the school year, both in-house and in premier performance spaces across New York City.

C.I.S 303 offers 45 minute art classes on a daily basis to 6th, 7th, and 8th grade students, for the duration of one marking period per year.  The art program follows the Blueprint for the Visual Arts Benchmarks outlined for specific grades and the Danielson's Framework for Teaching. Classes are designed to develop drawing, observation and analytical skills using varied media and the application of the Elements of Art. Units begin with classwork based on practice activities and progress to applications of techniques in hands-on projects. Works by renowned artists are introduced and end projects include the creation of original artwork. The goal of the art program is to teach skills that enable students to make connections across content areas and engage in self-expression. Students who demonstrate strong artistic potential and interest, are encouraged to pursue portfolio preparation for specialized high schools auditions. In addition after-school programs such as City Year help reinforce participation in the Visual Arts.

The Brooklyn High School of the Arts, now a district 15 school in downtown Brooklyn, boasts one of the most accomplished performing and fine arts programs in the City of New York. Our vocal/instrumental music program ranks among the finest in New York, and achieve top scores at state and city-wide competition annually. Our fine art program routinely wins major competitions, and has been featured in galleries across the country. It is a pipeline to major art universities here in New York and nationally. Our dance program, featured on Fox News is enjoying an energy that has our dance students accomplishing tremendous levels of performance. The spring dance concerts have become highlights of our school year. Our drama department, in its seventh year, featured a wonderful musical theater production of, "Once on this Island". Our Drama Department also starred in "Almost Maine". The performance was award winning, and we were one of only 4 schools featured in the Schubert Theatre on Broadway. The performance was also recognized by the Chancellor. " We are one of ten "Exploring the Arts/Tony Bennett" partner schools. ETA provides us with many opportunities for real world internships in the Arts for our students. In short, if you are interested in studying the arts in high school, and preparing for beyond, Brooklyn Arts is the school!

Our collaboration with Education Through Music continues to enhance our string instrumental program. The school orchestra has grown from 42 students in its first year to 92 students in our third year! This year the orchestra collaborated with One World Middle School in a holiday and Spring to the delight of students seeking admission to the school in sixth grade. P.S. 87 will join several schools across the City in an annual performance at Lehman College.  Our long term partnership with Studio in a School creates a vibrant visual arts environment.  Parents and students have also completed their second mural.  This mural, supported by a generous NYC Family Engagement grant, will be permanently installed in the lobby of our school. Our dance program is made possible by Music for Many and it was expanded this year to include Mary Poppins in Grade 2, Oliver in Grade 3 and Hip Hop in Grade 4. Grade 1 performance of Lion King World has become a school tradition.  Our Grade 3 chorus meets at 7 a.m. in the morning and the Grade 4 and 5 chorus meets during their lunch period once a week.  Music For Many has extended their support of our kindergarten students for the 2017-18 school year.

In addition to our premier seaside location, we are home to a state of the art dance studio, museum, art studio, well appointed auditorium and two technology labs. Our students are exposed to a myriad of enriching experiences including fine art, ballroom dance, modern, west african and jazz instruction, theater, chorus, violin study, photography and media arts. Annually, the dance and music presentations represent the culmination of student enrichment across the various arts disciplines. We believe such experiences allow P.S. 329 students to become empowered, inspired and elevated to their highest level of achievement!

We currently have an Arts Leadership Team comprised of students, teachers, and administrators. The team works towards our Arts Mission Statement and goals set early in the year. They organize programs, events and opportunities for both students and teachers around the arts. We highlight teacher strengths in the arts even if they are not certified as an arts teacher. Teachers take these strengths and create programs during and after-school in addition to sharing in teacher teams to build capacity in the arts. Our school environment consists of an arts gallery, "The Belmont Art Gallery," located in a hallway/bridge where all grades and programs are represented. Hallways, bulletin boards, and classrooms also come alive with arts. We have developed strong collaborations with our arts partners, particularly DreamYard, who have assisted in deepening the work around the arts disciplines.

The majority of Arts Programs rovided for our students happen thhrough our ater school partnership.  During the after school hours, students are engaged in Dance, Step, Voice and Theater. The art program at Mott Haven Village Preparatory High School incorporates movements in art history, famous artists from those movements, elements of art, and principles of design. Throughout the units of study, the students determine the importance in readings and complete numerous writing assignments including interpreting and analyzing artworks. The students participate in gallery walk activities and self/peer critiques. Our students produce work in areas such as but not limited to drawing, painting, and sculpture. Students produce a portfolio of completed work. They reflect on the progress made throughout the semester.

Our school's arts program is aligned with the requirements dictated by the Blueprint for the Arts, Danielson’s Framework for Teaching, English Language Arts, and the Mathematical Common Core Standards. Our goals are to create high standards for each student in our school and create a school environment that strongly supports the arts as an essential substance for child development. Our goal is to provide rigorous standard-based arts instruction that will contribute to our students’ college readiness. Our students are introduced to and given all the tools necessary to perform on a keyboard, reading musical notes, learn about the history of music in America and around the World. Students’ performance culminates with our concerts and recitals throughout the school year. Students are encouraged to perform in multiple forms of art such as theater and dance. We will continue working closely with our nonprofit organization partners, Music and the Brain and the Afro Latin Jazz Academy.

Classroom and out of classroom teachers engage students in arts instruction in alignment with the Blueprint for the Arts. Our students participate in visual arts activities such as painting, drawing, collage, and sculpture. Students learn about famous artists through read aloud, research and class discussions. Classroom teachers creatively connect drama and literacy by designing lessons where the children act out stories and put on plays. In addition, students engage in activities such as performing dance routines and drama skits for the students and parents of P.S. 222 to enjoy. Music and expressive movement are integrated into various curricula areas throughout the day. Teachers work collaboratively to produce grade level performances such as songfests and holiday shows. Every year our students participate in competitions where they can design books, posters, or create songs for the particular topic of the competition. We support our students’ talents and creativity by encouraging them to participate in a variety of contests.

Fine Arts Mission Statement 2016-2017. At the Bronx New School, the fine arts are a vital part of the comprehensive education plan for every student here. Our students learn skills in each of the arts areas in accordance to the New York City Blueprint for the Arts and New York State arts standards. Students learn how to make connections between the arts, academic subjects, and technology; building their creative and critical thinking skills, responsibility and self esteem. Students are also exposed to the many arts experiences that New York City has to offer by taking field trips several times a year to see live performances, art museums, and cultural centers. Students have the opportunity to display their work through performances and exhibitions for our school community in a number of celebrations through out the school year.

The High School for Environmental Studies provides students with opportunities to engage in the arts for all four years. In addition to offering our students beginning and advanced courses in chorus, orchestra, band and theater, we also offer ceramics, painting and drawing, as well as dance courses through a partnership with Alvin Ailey. HSES is a culturally rich community that enjoys a great deal of student involvement in our arts program. Our teachers are dedicated to providing our students with meaningful experiences and to exposing them to a wide array of art forms, including environmentally-themed arts projects.

Students at the Lab School will demonstrate independence and develop content knowledge through creative expression in the arts. Students are exposed to ballroom dancing in the 6th grade and Latin dancing in the 7th grade (for a quarter, as part of their physical education). KAPPA International High School provides a challenging and engaging arts curriculum. Our scholars are performers, composers, musicians and actors. We work with Shakespeareforum.org to provide free after-school drama lessons, culminating in an end of year performance.

Our goal is to provide all children with a well-rounded education. That entitlement requires introduction to, understanding of, and appreciation for the arts. Our goal is to increase the exposure of our students to the arts, giving students performance opportunities which will lead to increased listening, speaking, and motor skills. Additionally, by providing students with these experiences, they are also given the opportunity to find a talent within themselves.

We currently provide visual arts and dance through doe personnel. We also provide drama and theater through one outside organization, Enact Inc., which provide in-classroom workshops to our students on weekly basis.

Isaac Newton Middle School for Math and Science has a full time visual arts teacher and a drama teacher who does cycles of theatre for the sixth grade students. Students interested in applying for Visual Arts High Schools are given assistance and instruction on preparing their portfolios.

The Arts Program at P.S.90 offers a vibrant interdisciplinary approach to learning through our music and visual arts classes. All students receive instruction in the Visual Arts from either the school's licensed Art teacher or the Artist in Residence.   Students  participate in Borough wide and citywide contests and have the opportunity to have their work publicly displayed. This year, a Kindergarten student made it to the semi-finalist round of the P.S. Art competition. We also had a second grade student's artwork displayed at the Brooklyn Borough Arts Festival.        All students experience a vocal and instrumental music program which includes recorder, violin, keyboard and a complete Orff  orchestra. Our students receive Arts instruction in all the disciplines. We stage several performances every year. Brooklyn Institute for Liberal Arts now has a strong Arts program. We have a full-time art, music and theater teacher and our students are thriving.  Because of the continued support from Exploring the Arts (ETA), we were able to expand our arts program and bring in a vocal coach, a guitar coach, a percussionist and a graphic artist to work with the students. This year, we offered visual art classes to all of our students in grades 9-12. Students created numerous pieces of art, including self-portraits, which we put on display throughout the school. Our visual arts programs now include graphic design, print-making, and Photoshop. 
In music classes, students in all grades learned to play a variety of instruments and formed a school band. This band performs at our school concerts and other activities. We also have a chorus and a music production class for students who are interested in creating beats and writing music using technology.  We were finally able to get our Steel Pan Band up and running.  We were also able to offer theater classes to all 10th and 11th grade classes, and hired an organization called STEM for Dance to enable us to offer an even wider variety of classes to our students.

MS 324 provides a rigorous, Common Core State Standards based arts curriculum. It contains strong studio strands where students paint, draw, sing, act, dance, and play, as well as aesthetic education experiences that include learning about the art form in its context and in the world. Guided by the New York City Department of Education Curriculum Blueprint for Teaching and Learning in the Arts, students receive the unique arts experience of their New York City community. The curriculum focuses on five strands of instruction: Arts Making, Literacy in the Arts, Making Connections, Community and Cultural Resources and Careers and Lifelong Learning. Our goal is to give each student the opportunity to explore his or her creativity while integrating the arts across the content areas. With knowledge gained from prior residencies (Covenant Ballet Theatre of Brooklyn, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Making Books Sing, Education in Dance, Brooklyn Philharmonic and Midori & Friends) our teachers continue to use the arts as a vehicle to enhance the classroom curriculum and produce grade performances which include dance,music/singing,speaking & acting. We are continuing our Composer/Artist of the Month program in which the students are exposed to facts and musical excerpts each morning & we hope to include Dancer of the Month next year. Also, our certified arts teachers are utilizing specially equipped spaces such as the dance studio, art room & auditorium. This year we continued our music periods in which each grade meets together for instruction and the majority of our classes are receiving dance instruction as well. Our students can also participate in the arts by joining our after-school arts related clubs and through the Midori & Friends violin program. The arts are and will continue to be an integral part of PS 194.

The Marine Park Junior High Band Program has enjoyed many years of excellence. Located in Marine Park Brooklyn, students begin their musical day at 7:00 A.M. and often finish late in the evening. Students are taught their instruments from scratch in the 6th grade, and by 8th grade have several opportunities to thrive as young musicians. Marine Park's Band Program is comprised of beginner band, a symphonic band, two jazz ensembles (audition only), a marching band, and chorus. The symphonic band, jazz ensemble, jazz band and chorus have earned Gold and Gold with Distinction ratings at NYSSMA Festivals for the last seventeen years. Our Drama students are involved with two major productions each year. Our credits include Brighton Beach Memoirs, Lost in Yonkers, The Miracle Worker, Cinderella, Bye Bye Birdie, Little Shop of Horrors, Guys and Dolls, Fame Jr., To Kill A Mockingbird, Outsiders, Thoroughly Modern Millie, The Giver, and The Little Mermaid Jr.

q42_r1_c1: Learning through an Expanded Arts Program
q44_1: We provide arts integration within the Pre K - 5 curriculum. Both classroom teachers and certified art teacher provide experiences for students to use the arts as a catalyst for learning. Through collaboration and articulation, teachers create performance tasks cumulating in involving the multiple content disciplines. New opportunities from grant writing has allowed art to be a content area of learning in the after school program with Bronx Dance Theater. Students learn the dance steps for both ballet and jazz. Our many partnerships with other organization has helped us strengthen and maintain our focus on the arts. Organizations include: American Ballroom Dancing, NY Botanical Garden, Young People's Chorus, LEAP, Bronx Arts Ensemble and Ballet Hispanico.

P.S 109 is servicing grades 3-8 in Visual Arts. This year P.S 109 provided the students with instruction in painting, drawing, pastel art, mixed-media and sculpture. Cross-curriculum information was incorporated into each visual art lesson, and each unit plan was tied to a specific artist and art period. ART CLUB was offered every day during lunch in order to facilitate the students with High school portfolio preparation, and the development of personal art interest exploration. As a result two students got into the specialized art high schools of their choice. Students were provided with differentiated visual and physical materials in order to reach their diverse learning styles. Students work was exhibited in the Annual District 22 art show. Additionally, students were entered into the Annual Brooklyn MLK arts competition where two of of them won first and second place.
P.S 109 is currently working with an art partnership called "Studio in a School" students are exploring pottery making and clay sculpture design from a teaching artist.  With the skills gained through this partnership, next year we would like  to incorporate more clay sculpture making into the art curriculum at P.S 109. Additionally, we would like to incorporate more technology and digital visual art based lessons into our program.

We provide programs in Dance, Photography, film Production, Digital Arts, Cartooning, Guitar and Sound engineering (a new course).  One goal for Film Production and Sound Engineering is to prepare students to pass industry certifications exams.

The goals for the CS 150 Arts Program is to increase the number of programs offered. The Art Program will also work in conjunction with outside organizations to support and enhanced our students cognitive skills, and develop a collaborative environment for our students through the program.  The Art Program will facilitate students to use problem solving skills to find to find solutions to adverse issues in the arts and also in their lives.  Students will be able to exhibit a mean of self expression through the arts and share those skills with the school community.  With the aide of the New York Blue Print for the Arts, students will be able to meet the standards by exploring the essential elements needed for monitoring their learning experience.  This can be done through formative assessment strategies and set criteria to improve students achievement/learning goals.  Clear criteria will be implemented where students will be using language specific for the blueprints for learning. Students will use these standards to connect to the common core standards and develop various components to complete projects and become lifelong learners in the world.

The arts at PS 58 provide a rich and diverse experience for all students. Students receive instruction from highly qualified arts teachers in music, visual arts and drama. While there is no dance teacher employed full time the curriculum is enriched by collaborations with cultural institutions such as Dancing Classrooms and The New York City Ballet. The lower grade music program is built upon instruction of percussion, visual work and beginning notation. In the upper grades the music curriculum centers around students in grades three through five learning to read musical notation and playing a string instrument of their choice. In the visual arts - exploration of media, visualization and problem solving skills are developed over the six years that students receive instruction. The visual arts program relies heavily on visiting artists, contemporary designs, interdisciplinary learning and technology in the arts. Each year, all PS58 students showcase a piece of their artwork during the weeklong Annual Art Show. The Drama program uses scripted work and improvisation to teach students about the theatre. Classes put on small productions throughout the year. The fifth grade class culminates their program with a major performance. The Arts continue to be a stronghold in our school supported and loved by all students, teachers, school leaders, families and the entire community.

Located in the heart of historic Greenwich Village, PS41 both reflects the rich cultural diversity of our neighborhood, and dynamically incorporates the resources of our neighborhood into our studies. The arts are integrated into all curriculum areas. Our building is a vibrant testimony to the creative pulse of our community. We ahve partnerships with: National Dance Institute, the Highline, the Whitney Museum and Lincoln Center.

Grant Avenue Elementary School is committed to the arts as a critical way in which our students learn more about the world and more about themselves. Our students experience quality visual arts, and music instruction throughout the school year with our specialty teachers. Students receive additional arts instruction from cultural organizations across the city including Studio in a School, Story Pirates, and Third Street Music School Settlement thanks in large part to our partnership with Change for Kids. We pride ourselves on engaging with parents through the arts and, together, we celebrate our talented students and showcase their work at annual musical performance events (concerts and a 5th grade musical) and one major art exhibition each year.

We presently offer visual arts and Orchestra. Our goal is to provide our diverse population with opportunities to explore the different art forms, the integration of the arts using an interdisciplinary approach across content area thus  following the common core curriculum. It is our plan to offer digital arts  and dance for the 2017-2018 school year.  

Our Arts program continues to allow students to develop creatively and challenge their knowledge of style, artists and cultural contributions to the world of the Arts. We support the individual talents that students posses in music performance, music theory and visual arts. We accomplish this through integration of curriculum across the content areas; we maintain high expectations through standards based education. Keeping with the common core standards math and literacy continue to play an important role. As students use skills in measurement, experimentation, reading comprehension, expand vocabulary and defending opinions through arguments while exposed to a variety of text, visual representations lead student discussion and dialogue as they acquire meaning. We prepare students during the middle school years to be armed with the tools and achievement expectation that will afford them successful paths in high school and college.

q44_1: In an effort to have students learn to express themselves visually, many projects are designed to be reflective of each student. Projects are aimed to allow students to be reflective and express who they are as individuals.  Students use the elements of art and the principles of design to build upon their understanding of art, as well as the artistic process.  In order to gain a deeper understanding of successful works of art, each project will highlight a particular principle and/or element.

New Design is a design education focused high school which includes design courses offered in 10th - 12th grades. Courses offered include 10th Grade Foundations to Design, Fashion Design and Advance Fashion Design, Graphic Design and Entrepreneurial Design. Students can also enroll in Art Portfolio classes to assist them in applying to Art and Design colleges and programs.

We have added an AP art to the curriculum. In addition, we added painting courses to our art curriculum and have incoporated the Common Core Standards into our lessons. We continue to offer studio art and introduction to art courses as well.

P.S. 140's goals for our schools' art programs focus on coordinating the planning between the classroom teachers, the music teacher, part-time visual arts teacher and visiting artists in order to integrate the arts and curriculum to have a more positive impact on student learning. We look forward to building on the addition of the visual arts program through the Arts Matters initiative this past year. We expect that this initiative will inspire and encourage students to gain skills and confidence through art and galleries. In addition, we will continue to enhance our school environment and culture by encouraging performances and displays that not only celebrate the talents of our students but also create more of a connection and understanding of the various units of study in different curriculum areas. We currently and consistently have student work on display throughout our school building. This enables students to support each other and gain respect for each others work and skills. In addition, we have a middle school art gallery and photography wall which showcases the art work and photography created by our middle school students in collaboration with our community based arts organizations.
q45_1: We did not receive 21st Century Grant, as we had for the past 14 years, that supported the arts program at M140.  Budget does not allow for M140 to sustain many, and possibly all partnerships with Arts organizations.

At I.S.289, the arts program is both embedded in the project based curriculum, and as part of a stand alone comprehensive visual arts and music program.  

Within the project based curriculum of each core class, students use the digital and visual arts to engage in the culture and texts of the content, as well as to demonstrate understanding of the content. 

Within the Visual Arts and Music curriculum, the five strands include the various types of art and music making, developing art and music literacy, making connections to the world and to other disciplines through music and the visual arts, exploring careers in music and the arts, and learning about community and cultural resources.

q42_r1_c1: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
q44_1: We continue to work closely with our art teacher to ensure that he has the resources to develop student skills and to engage them in projects that challenge their abilities in the realm of visual arts. Additionally, we have noted student enthusiasm and requests and have subsequently expanded our art program to include an after school art club. This program allows students to continue working on various class projects after school or to engage themselves in a special project designed for the group by our art teacher. We have installed a Mac lab and have begun the process of introducing students to photography and graphic design skills. We have also created a music program that is conducted twice a week during the students’ lunch period and after school. This program has been expanded to include instruction with musical instruments. Based upon the level of student participation, we hope to continue and to expand this program still further.

All students at IHSL receive three full years of arts instruction, including visual arts and media arts in the 9th/10th grades as well as multi-media music arts in the 12th grade. All students will have access to additional arts offerings (singing, dance, film/media, photography) through our elective program. Also, the arts program at IHSL has designed innovative, interdisciplinary curricula for ELLs. Additionally, extensive outreach is done to partnership organizations to provide additional opportunities to students, based on need and interest.

P.S. 971 continues to provide an educationally enriched arts. In our dance, visual arts, music and theatre programs, students are able to express their individual creativity while further deepening the connection between performing, visual and musical arts. In addition, to further reinforce the students' understanding of arts, Brooklyn Conservatory of Music returned this year. As a result, this musical program helps students explore musical enrichment through hands-on participation in musical instruments, cultural songs and rhythmic applications. PS 971 students also enjoy in-house performances through Lincoln Center, where they are instructed about the history and evolution of Jazz. In addition, students have opportunities to experience art in technology with our partnerships in Robotics and Coding. Building upon last years success, the coding and robotics program has expanded to include an after school component. PS 971 students explore primary sources that include art artifacts for study and reflection. As a whole, while following the Blue Print for the Arts Standards, students are able to explore the connection with the arts throughout their daily content areas programs.

The P.S. 64 Arts program makes constant efforts to provide a range of artistic and cultural experiences throughout grade levels. The Students receive focused visual arts lessons from a certified fine art education teacher who also holds a masters degree in fine arts. The students receive instruction one to three times a week through the entire school year. The art facilities are well suited for a wide range of medium; Painting, Sculpture, printmaking, life drawing, and collage are all part of the curriculum. The classroom teacher and visual arts teacher integrate curriculum to foster richer learning. The art curriculum also focuses on the benchmarks set through the blueprint for the arts. Theater, music and dance are also provided to the students by outside cultural organizations. Professionals from within the fields of music, dance, and theater, provide direct instruction to students in these content areas.

The PS 106 school community continues to strengthen in our ongoing effort to provide a well-rounded arts education program. Our teachers are passionate about education and our belief in arts education as a key component in every child's learning. Collaboration among students, staff and parents is the foundation for supporting student learning in all areas. Our common goal is to escalate student participation, heighten best practices in teaching and include parents and community in our partnership for an exemplary arts education program. We also work in collaboration with available artist residency programs to expose our students to as much culture and experience in the arts as possible. This year our residency programs included Studio in a School, Dancing Classrooms, Park Avenue Armory, and Disney Kids. Each of these experiences allows students to make connections between the arts while applying depth of knowledge in core subjects, including Language Arts, Math and Social Studies.Together, our teachers are working to help our students to grow creatively and intellectually, while having positive experiences for self-expression.

Children learn to perceive and respond to works of art. Children also involve themselves in looking, touching, and analyzing the visual aspects of their environment. Art education is primarily connected with visual experiences. Kindergarten thru Grade 5 students are capable of creating, perceiving and discussing the visual arts.
q45_1: 90% of our Arts programming has come from the Extended School Day/Violence Prevention Program. Extended School Day/Violence Prevention Program was awarded during the 2016/2017 school year.

q44_1: The Charles A. Dorsey School provides comprehensive Common Core Aligned cultural arts experiences for our scholars. Through the arts, students acquire tools to engage with a range of source materials and learn to draw on research to investigate their own families and cultural traditions in order to express ideas about the world through the arts.

Hiring a music teacher this year who had been an Arts Education Liaison for 7 years gave P.S. 161X not only a seasoned arts instructor but also one who was privy to the panoply of programs and grants offered by the Office of Arts and Special Programs and local community-based partnerships.  Our principal created space for arts professional development and interdepartmental inquiries to determine what resources were needed to bolster student learning and encourage student creativity.  

This year our school was awarded a grant to renovate our auditorium stage.  With new lighting and sound systems, students with cognitive, auditory, visual, and locomotor deficits will have new pathways to gain agency over their decision-making and have greater access to performances that would previously have been unavailable to them. 

In line with the school-wide instructional focus on reading this year, students in the music room have focused on music-making, particularly around literacy.  Using the Blueprint for the Arts and the Danielson Framework, this was implemented through student-led discussion, group ensemble playing, and language acquisition within reading music notation.  Experiential objectives have also been prioritized through arts field trips and in-house performances.

Next year we will be build an inquiry team with Lincoln Center Education to look into how the arts can bolster language acquisition among English Language Learning students.

Public School 315 is widely recognized as a school where the successful integration of arts education , academics and quality teaching are lifting student achievement. P.S. 315 has built an exemplary curriculum that emphasizes both arts integration and sequential skills-based instruction in dance, music, visual arts and theater. Literacy, social studies, computer graphics and science all have art components taught by classroom teachers and academic clusters. The arts specialists all integrate literacy, social studies and science disciplines into their curriculum. The efforts of the teachers are reinforced by partnerships with a team of preeminent cultural institutions. It is the school’s philosophy that through the emergence of the arts, students will make valuable contributions to the community.
q45_1: This year we were at a detriment regarding our Arts Programs. Our auditorium has been off limits from January through the present. It is the process of being repaired. We are a shared campus and did not have access to a large space as we had to share the gymnasium for the lunch periods as well as the gym periods for both schools. Our Arts Program will hopefully make a comeback for the 2017-18 school year.

q44_1: This marks another year of working with Education Through Music. It continues to be a great success and end of year shows continue to demonstrate great growth in our students.  This year, we were accepted into the Broadway Junior Program and we were able to produce our very first musical. This musical allowed all of our students to play a vital role( set design, costume design, dancers, singers, actors, lighting crew, stage crew, stage managers, etc)  This opportunity really exposed our students to new endeavors. Also Dancing Classrooms came and visited our school for the first time.  Our students were able to be apart of an actual competition as well. They met with each of our 8th grade classes for 45 minutes once a week for 20 weeks.  Awesome experience. I believe they will be returning next year.

Our art program is in the budding stage. We brought on a new art teacher and she has been able to infuse visual arts across the disciplines and has created some amazing art projects with students. One project was featured at the Bronx Museum of the Arts!

Our school collaborated with our neighboring small school to provide Visual Arts and Music classes to students through the support of the High School Arts Matters funding.  Students were exposed to music theory concepts and visual arts open studio activities that offered them exposure to techniques.

q42_r1_c1: BRIC Arts Media Bklyn Inc.Brooklyn Information & Culture ROTUNDA
q44_1: Selected classes in grades pre-K through grade eight receive visual arts education at least 50 minutes per week. All grade five and grade eight students receive arts integration a minimum of 200 minutes per week. Selected students in grades pre-k through five receive instruction in ballet, recorder, violin, and piano. To supplement the arts program during the day, Sports in Arts School Foundation provides additional instruction in African dance, stepping, drumming, theatre, and martial arts for students in grades 5 through 8.

P.S. 5: The Ellen Lurie School is the winner of the prestigious Leonore Annenberg School Fund for Children grant. In partnership with the Center for Arts Education, the grant allows for the planning and implementation of extensive music-integrated curricula for all students in grades PreK-5. Our goal is to encourage our students to use their imaginations to solve problems by nourishing their creative skills. We believe the arts provide entry points into Common Core Learning Standards-aligned curriculum for students and are a vehicle for students to build self-confidence by feeling successful in the classroom and can be a catalyst for increased student motivation and achievement. We are committed to hiring certified arts teachers to lead our arts programming, with a focus on visual arts. We strive to meet the NYS instructional time requirements. In order to allow learning within all four arts disciplines, we partner with cultural organizations, including the Center for Arts Education, Shen Wei Dance Arts, and Studio in a School. Through these partnerships, students not only reap the benefits of an enriched curriculum, but teachers also have the opportunity to grow professionally through planning and delivering instruction in cooperation with teaching artists, thereby expanding their capacity to integrate the arts throughout the school day for our students. P.S. 5 expands our arts offerings after school, through two select choral groups, xylophone ensemble, ELL visual arts / science program and a family arts program.

NYC Lab Middle School for Collaborative Studies works to provide a comprehensive arts experience connected to all subject areas and in arts specific courses of study. In sixth grade students participate in a year-long introduction to visual arts with a focus on drawing, stop-motion animation and visual communication through art. In seventh grade students take drama. Students engage in playwriting, learn acting techniques and have opportunities to perform. The seventh grade course is designed in collaboration with a partnership at The New Victory Theater. In eighth grade students study visual arts through a survey of fine arts. A partnership with The Whitney Museum helps support this work. Students in eighth grade visit the museum multiple times throughout the year. A museum educator also works with students at the school site. The students also showcase art work at a culminating show in the museum. Arts is integral to the student experience at NYC Lab Middle School for Collaborative Studies. We have prioritized arts education - providing nearly double the required amount to our students. We believe that when students are allowed to engage in art making and learning about art they grow as learners and human beings.
